s: a male given name, popular currently in Germany
Maximilian.et: Saint's name from Latin Maximilianus, a derivative of Maximus "the greatest". It was used in German royal houses after Friedrich III chose it for his son in 1459, explaining it as a combination of the names of two Roman generals, Maximus and Aemilianus.

s: an a popular diminutive of the male given name Maximilian

Maxime.et: From French maxime, from Latin maximē.

Maximalpigmentierter.et: Literally, “maximally pigmented person”. maximal (“maximal(ly)”) + pigmentiert (“pigmented”), from pigmentieren (“to pigment”), perhaps coined as an imitation of politically correct terminology.

s: a female given name, feminine of Maximilian
placeholder name used on samples and forms: John Q. Public, John Doe (but not used in legal contexts)
Max Mustermann.et: Max (common German given name) + Mustermann (placeholder surname, literally “Sampleman, Exampleman”).

Maxillarpalpus.et: Calque of New Latin palpus maxillaris. By surface analysis, maxillar (“maxillary”) + Palpus (“palp”).
